Following:
 La.App. Nos. 527/2013 & 135 Of 2014
 3
 2025:Ker:40772
 Judgment
1.  These two appeals arise from the judgment in LAR No.24/1999 under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
The Claimant, as well as the Requisitioning Authority, has come up by filing Appeal.
Appellant in L.A.A.No.527/2013/claimant seeks enhancement of compensation.
Appellant in L.A.A.No.135/2014/Requisitioning Authority challenges the enhancement given by the Reference Court.

2. An extent of 1.62 Ares of land comprised in Survey No.1300/1- 7 of Thrissur village, belonging to the claimant/Trust, was acquired as per 4(1) Notification dated 08.08.1994 under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 for road widening.
The Land Acquisition Officer awarded compensation fixing the land value @ Rs.36,600/- per cent.
On reference, the Reference LA.APP. NOS. 527/2013 & 135 OF 2014 2025:KER:40772 Court awarded compensation fixing the land value at Rs.1,10,000/- per cent.

3. I heard the learned Counsel for the claimant, Sri. Jawahar Jose, Standing Counsel for the Thrissur Municipality/Requisitioning Authority, Sri. Santhosh Poduval, and the learned Senior Government Pleader for the State, Smt. Rekha C. Nair.
4.
The learned counsel for the claimant contended that the Reference Court acted illegally in discarding Ext.A1 document.
Ext.A1 document relates to the adjacent property.
As per Ext.A1, 19 cents of land was sold for an amount of Rs.80,00,000/-.
The value per cent would come to Rs.4,21,052/-.

The Reference Court ought to have awarded compensation relying on Ext.A1, if necessary, by making necessary deduction from Ext.A1 on account of the time difference between Section 4(1) Notification and the date of Ext.A1 document.
There is no evidence to show that a building LA.APP. NOS. 527/2013 & 135 OF 2014 2025:KER:40772 was situated therein in Ext.A1 property
. Admittedly, the property is situated in a prime location in Thrissur city.
At any rate, the land value awarded by the Reference Court is on the lower side.
The circumstances under which Ext.A1 document was executed were explained by AWs 1 & 3, who are the seller and the purchaser.
No question challenging the correctness of the transaction in Ext.A1 document and the value therein was put to those witnesses.
The learned counsel concluded his argument, praying to fix the land value relying on Ext.A1 document.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Requisitioning Authority contended that the acquired property is situated within the Thrissur Municipality.
The claimant has produced only one document, which is a post-Notification document.
In a city like Thrissur, there will be ever so many pre-Notification documents showing the land value.

No such document was produced LA.APP. NOS.
527/2013 & 135 OF 2014 2025:KER:40772 before the Reference Court.
The production of only one post- notification document itself creates suspicion with regard to the transaction covered by Ext.A1 document.
6. The learned Senior Government Pleader also supported the arguments made by the Requisitioning Authority.
7. I have considered the rival contentions.
8. The Section 4(1) Notification in this case is dated 08.08.1994.
Ext.A1 document is dated 17/03/1995.
The claimant has produced only one document to prove the land value.
The Reference Court has found that it is a post-notification document and the value of structures therein is not separately shown.
As rightly pointed out by the learned counsel for the Requisitioning Authority, the production of only one document, which is a post-Notification document, itself is suspicious.
In a city like Thrissur, there would have been ever so many pre-Notification documents to prove the land value in LA.APP. NOS. 527/2013 & 135 OF 2014 2025:KER:40772 the city.

Even if the documents of the adjacent properties are not available, the other documents in the very same city could have been produced for comparison of the land value as on the date of the Section 4(1) Notification.
The question of placing reliance on post-Notification arises only if pre-Notification documents are not available.
The acquisition and consequent road widening and developments might have caused a sudden increase in the land value after the acquisition.

Since Section 4(1) Notification is of the year 1994, at this distance of time, this Court is not even able to do any guess work with respect to the land value available in the area in which the acquired property is situated.
Hence, the prayer of the Counsel for the claimant to grant land value based on Ext.A1 is rejected.
9. The evidence on record would reveal that the acquired property is situated in a prime commercial area.

The Reference Court has relied on Serial No.3 Document in Ext R2 (a) in which the LA.APP.
NOS. 527/2013 & 135 OF 2014 2025:KER:40772 land value is Rs.97,600/-.
The Reference Court has specifically found that when compared to the said document, the acquired land is in a more advantageous location as much as it faces two roads on the south and the west.
It is in evidence that the Post Office Road is more important than Chemboth Lane.
The acquired property is having frontage to Post Office Road also.

When the Reference Court found that the acquired property is more advantageous and has frontage of two roads when compared to Serial No.3 Document in Ext.
R2(a), the Reference Court ought to have given more enhancement than the value fixed in the impugned judgment.
I am of the opinion that the Reference Court ought to have fixed the land value at Rs.1,25,000/- per cent for the acquired land.
Hence, LAA No.135/2014 filed by the Requisitioning Authority is liable to be dismissed and LAA No.527/2013 filed by the claimant is liable to be allowed fixing the land value at LA.APP.
